summary: Full text of the 2021 Nutrients meta-analysis (13 crossover RCTs in athletes, acute caffeine 1-9 mg/kg in capsules, drinks, gum, bars) shows better attention accuracy and speed in very small pooled analyses, with no effect on reaction time or inhibitory control; it gets one eligible context with mixed results recorded, for the record's Focus & Mental Clarity claim. The 3-km run RCT is abstract-only and gets no credit. The umbrella review and strength meta-analysis had no open full text, so they are recorded without credit.

applicability.studied_population: Adult athletes given acute caffeine (mostly 1-6 mg/kg) before or during exercise in 13 randomized crossover studies; pooled attention accuracy and speed improved, reaction time and inhibitory control did not.

identity.preparation: Oral caffeine in drinks, capsules, bars or gum; some formulations include carbohydrate or other ingredients.

population.description: 13 randomized crossover studies in adult athletes (194 participants: 158 men, 36 women; professional to recreational rugby, soccer, cycling, golf, shooting, team-sport and resistance-trained subjects); 5 studies (18 trials) entered the meta-analysis. Ill, injured and non-adult participants excluded.

study_contexts.study_design: PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of double/single-blind randomized placebo-controlled crossover studies (August 1999-March 2020); Hedges' g/SMD pooling, mostly fixed-effect; only objective cognitive measures meta-analysed.

outcomes.name: Attention: accuracy SMD 1.07 (95% CI 0.16 to 1.98), p=0.02 (2 trials, 24 participants); response speed SMD -1.41 (-2.65 to -0.17), p=0.03 (2 trials).

Simple reaction time SMD -0.05 (-0.59 to 0.49), p=0.86; choice reaction time SMD -0.69 (-1.15 to 0.17), p=0.12; inhibitory-control accuracy SMD 0.19 (-0.61 to 1.00), p=0.64 and speed SMD -0.31 (-1.12 to 0.50), p=0.45.
Self-reported energy, focus, mood and RPE (narrative, Table 6): improvements in some studies, none in others.

limitations: Sports-cognition findings do not establish universal cognition or product benefit.
Do not attribute combination effects to caffeine alone or treat bodyweight-based doses as fixed capsule thresholds.

Returned A052 'source-content hold for each intended outcome' is resolved for this source by full-text verification; credit is limited to focus/attention during exercise in athletes.

Very small pooled analyses (2 trials, about 24 participants for attention); reaction time and inhibitory control did not improve; no primary outcome designated (hierarchy not_reported). One included study used a caffeine mouthwash (not ingestion) and several used carbohydrate co-exposure.
Findings are in young, mostly male athletes during exercise; they do not establish general cognitive enhancement or energy benefit in non-athletes.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Acute single or repeated pre-/during-exercise doses, mostly 30-60 min before testing (range 5-90 min; some repeated every 13-55 min during exercise) (Results 3.3).
co_therapies: Carbohydrate co-exposure in some arms (carbohydrate solution, energy bar, 7% carbohydrate mouthwash); TeaCrine comparison arms in two studies were not part of the caffeine-versus-placebo contrast; exercise protocols differ.
dose.reported_regimen: Doses below 1 or above 9 mg/kg excluded; studies used <3 mg/kg (4), 3-6 mg/kg (8) or 2 and 4 mg/kg (1); examples 4.1 mg/kg gum, 5-6 mg/kg capsules, 275-300 mg capsules, 100 mg in a 45 g carbohydrate bar, 67 mg/25 mL mouthwash (Tables 5-6). No scalar pooled dose.

normalization.basis: A heterogeneous synthesis has no single assigned-arm dose. Descriptive regimens do not create an intake recommendation, equivalent preparation or efficacy threshold.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC8000732): Methods 2.1-2.5 (PICOS Table 1, exclusions), Results 3.3 (dose, vehicle, timing), 3.5 meta-analysis paragraphs, Tables 5-6, Discussion limitations, funding/COI.

identity.preparation: Caffeine 3 mg/kg body mass (vehicle not reported in the abstract).

study_contexts.study_design: Double-blind randomized crossover: placebo versus caffeine before a 3-km outdoor track run.

dose.administration_frequency: Single acute dose before the run.
dosage_forms: oral caffeine (vehicle not reported in the abstract)
dose.reported_regimen: 3 mg/kg body mass caffeine or placebo, single acute dose.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract; full text not open access.

outcomes.name: 3-km time improved 1.1% versus placebo (10.13 +/- 0.69 vs 10.25 +/- 0.72 min, p<0.001); attention +15.6% (p<0.001), reaction time +5.9% (p<0.05); feeling scale improved.
Oxidative stress markers: no caffeine effect.

limitations: Abstract only: vehicle, timing, primary-outcome designation and methods could not be verified, so the context carries no credit.
Single small crossover (n=13); body-weight dose is not a fixed capsule amount.
